sections.en: Total market capitalization stands near $1,720.9B (CoinGecko). Reported 24-hour spot volume is $27.93B with 7-day average turnover broadly normal versus the trailing month (0.93x) . Note: the sentiment reading above is the public alternative.me series; proprietary on-chain datasets are still left out rather than estimated. The alternative.me Fear & Greed gauge prints 73 (Greed).

**Derivatives positioning.** The public Binance futures endpoints did not answer for this asset on this cycle, so rather than fabricate a view the desk flags it as a **data gap**: funding and open-interest extremes remain the standard trigger for squeeze dynamics in Bitcoin.

**Trend structure.** Across horizons the picture is perfect bullish alignment (price > EMA20 > EMA50 > EMA200), the textbook configuration of a trend-following regime where pullbacks into the 20-day mean tend to be bought. Spot at $85,640 versus EMA20 $83,279, EMA50 $79,138 and EMA200 $75,531 frames the medium-term bias mechanically rather than emotionally. From this configuration the desk's working assumption is that trend-following exposure is only justified while price holds the side of the 50-day average it currently occupies.

**Key levels.** The operational map reads: initial support at $84,853 (recent swing low); the lower Bollinger band $77,708 as the 2σ downside envelope; first resistance at $86,172 (recent swing high); upper band $89,010 as the stretch target. Levels derived from the last ~60 sessions of closes are guides for location, not promises of reaction; they mark where prior two-way business was done and therefore where resting liquidity is most plausible. ATR(14) of $2,094 implies a typical daily range of roughly 2.4 percent of spot, which is the unit of risk to size positions against.

**Momentum.** RSI(14) prints 64.1 — neutral territory; MACD (12/26/9) sits below its signal line (1983 vs 2059, histogram -76.1), consistent with fading momentum. Momentum readings are state descriptors, not trade signals on their own; the desk treats confluence between momentum and level location as the actionable unit.

**Volatility & liquidity.** 30-day realized volatility annualizes near 38%; the 20-day band spans 14% of the mid — compressed, which often precedes a volatility expansion; 7-day turnover runs at 0.93x the trailing-month norm. Behavior around these regimes — absorption at band edges, volume confirmation on breaks — is what separates a tradeable move from noise.

**Performance context.** On longer windows the asset has returned +7.29% over 30 days and +35.30% over 90 days. Positioning decisions made on monthly horizons should respect these base rates instead of extrapolating the last week. The 7-session change (+2.56%) is the shortest window the desk treats as signal rather than noise.

sections.en: Independent cross-check — TradingView's technical vote on BTC (1d): 13 buy / 10 neutral / 3 sell of the standard indicator set, summing to Buy; oscillators Neutral, moving averages Strong Buy. A crowd-signal quoted alongside, not in place of, the local computation above.

**Bullish scenario.** Continuation higher requires acceptance above $86,172 on expanding turnover; continued holds of the 50-day average ($79,138); RSI holding above 60 (currently 64). Under those conditions the path of least resistance flips to buy-the-dip, with prior resistance converting to support as the confirmation test.

**Bearish scenario.** Downside continuation triggers on a decisive loss of $84,853. In that case failed support typically becomes the new ceiling, and momentum chasers provide the exit liquidity.

Net take on Bitcoin: spot $85,635 with the medium-term bias constructive while price holds the relevant side of the 50-day average. The 24-hour tape (+0.03%) is consistent with that bias. Decision zones are the levels named in the technical section, not opinions: trade the reaction at those prices, not the headline of the day.
